paras: It was the hottest summer anyone could remember. The ponds had dried into cracked mud, and the streams had shrunk to nothing. High above the fields, a crow flew from tree to tree, searching for a single drop of water. His throat burned and his wings felt heavy.

At last, near a farmer's hut, he saw a clay pitcher standing in the shade. His heart leapt. He landed on its rim and peered inside. There was water, but only a little, far down at the bottom. He pushed his beak in as far as it would go, yet he could not reach it.

The crow tried to tip the pitcher over, but it was too heavy. He hopped around it, cawing in frustration. For a moment he thought of flying away. Then he noticed the small pebbles scattered on the ground nearby.

An idea sparkled in his mind. He picked up a pebble in his beak and dropped it into the pitcher. Plop! Then another. Plop! And another. With each pebble, the water rose a little higher. The crow worked patiently, pebble after pebble, though the sun beat down on his back.

Slowly the water climbed up, up, up, until at last it shimmered just below the rim. The crow dipped his beak and drank deeply, and the cool water soothed his dry throat. Refreshed, he spread his wings and flew back into the bright sky.
Moral: Where there is a will, there is a way. Patience and clear thinking can solve problems that strength alone cannot.
